clue.text: Impression, not good, full of mostly rubbish ability to produce desired results

indicators.note: 'full of' means the shortened likeness is filled with the trimmed slang word
'not' tells us the letter for good is dropped from the likeness

parts.note: an effigy is an image or likeness, an impression of a person

indicators.note: 'mostly' means the slang word for rubbish loses its final letter

parts.note: cack is British slang for rubbish

explanation.surface: A review of some work: the impression it left was bad, stuffed with rubbish, lacking any ability to achieve results.
explanation.walkthrough: Cack is coarse British slang for rubbish or excrement; 'Impression' looks like a feeling but is a likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficacy is the power to bring about an intended effect, exactly the capacity described.

clue.text: Company allowance should cover close to ceremony

indicators.note: one word covering another means wrapping round it, so the ration encloses the short word

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
on can mean close to or adjacent, as in 'a house on the river'

explanation.surface: A firm's spending allowance ought to pay for the end of some ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronation is the formal ritual of crowning a monarch, a grand state occasion.

clue.text: Substitute in centre of goal, jumping up, scored in time

indicators.note: 'in' places the stand-in inside the middle letters
in a down clue, jumping up means the letters read from bottom to top
'centre of' takes the inner letters of goal

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, a substitute

explanation.surface: A football report: a substitute in the goalmouth leaps and scores in the nick of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' points to music: A TEMPO is a direction written in a score meaning return to the original speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'in time', a marking that composers put in printed music to restore the earlier speed.

clue.text: Original form of tyre containing carbon

indicators.note: 'containing' means the tyre word holds the chemical symbol inside it

parts.note: a radial is a type of tyre with cords running across the tread
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a novel tyre design built around carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical can mean fundamental or innovative, departing from the old: an original new idea.

clue.text: Food shop cutting unusually fine pasta

indicators.note: the shop name cuts into the jumbled letters, splitting them
'unusually' signals that the letters of fine appear in an odd order

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared food

explanation.surface: A delicatessen slicing some unusually thin pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges FINE as FENI, and DELI cuts it in two: FE-DELI-NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fedelini are a very thin Italian noodle, a variety of spaghetti-like strand.

clue.text: Goddess having gravitas, on and off

indicators.note: taking letters on and off means picking every other one, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A deity whose dignity comes and goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaia is the Greek earth deity, mother of the Titans.

clue.text: A girl left cracking info on 50s hairstyle?

indicators.note: 'cracking' means breaking into the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a DA (duck's arse) was a 1950s greased-back men's haircut

explanation.surface: A girl breaking a story about a retro haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the hairstyle below GLEN in this down entry. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenda is a female first name, so it is an example of what a girl might be called.

clue.text: Female pro in sci-fi classic struggle

indicators.note: 'in' puts the female and pro letters inside the film title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's classic science-fiction film
for means in favour of, as pro does

explanation.surface: A woman professional battling within a science-fiction classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort means strenuous exertion, a hard attempt or battle to achieve something.

clue.text: Last word associated with clever subject

parts.note: amen is said at the very end of a prayer
able means skilled or clever

explanation.surface: Having the final say is linked with being a bright topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' is an adjective here, as in 'subject to the law', not a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable to rules means liable or answerable to them, the same as subject to them.

clue.text: See you love following spies overseas

indicators.note: 'following' places the zero after the agency's letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US foreign intelligence agency
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A farewell note from a sweetheart tracked by foreign agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an informal Italian farewell, used in English as a casual goodbye.

clue.text: Unanimated, sad relative

indicators.note: 'sad' here suggests a sorry, messed-up state of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lifeless, gloomy family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unanimated, sad' looks like a description of the relative; the first word is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden aunt is an unmarried aunt, an older female family member.

clue.text: Cut back, catching horse by a curved path

indicators.note: 'catching' means the reversed word encloses the horse
'back' means the word for cut is read from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: Something trimmed back, snaring a horse beside a winding route.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is the curve a thrown object traces, the path of a projectile.

clue.text: Where cast is perhaps not in touch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the actors are in a play
second meaning: a ball not over the touchline is still live in the game

explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby 'touch' is the area beyond the side lines; a ball there is out of play.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both actors appearing on stage and a ball still live in a match.

clue.text: Marshal urged fire power up-front, having thought ahead?

indicators.note: 'up-front' puts the power letter at the start, at the top of this down entry

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military marshal urging firepower forward, with a plan in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a rank; it is the anagram signal for URGED FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefigure is to imagine or foreshadow something beforehand, a form of anticipating.

clue.text: Effusive, your current name finally put forward

indicators.note: the final letter of the assembled string is moved to the front

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
to call is to name

explanation.surface: Someone gushing that your name in use now has at last been put up as a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: YR + I + CALL gives YRICALL; moving its last L to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical can mean expressing enthusiasm in a gushing, poetic way, as in 'waxing lyrical'.

clue.text: A prayer made in moonwalk, maybe over lunar seas

indicators.note: 'over' signals turning the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: EVA (extravehicular activity) is a spacewalk, of which a moonwalk is an example
maria are the dark plains on the moon, Latin for seas

explanation.surface: An astronaut praying during a moonwalk above the moon's seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria (Hail Mary) is a Catholic devotion addressed to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Ragamuffin essentially suppressing tact

indicators.note: the two words hold down the answer within them, keeping it concealed

explanation.surface: A scruffy urchin basically keeping a lid on diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicacy and skill in handling people, a refined subtlety.

clue.text: My sons possibly absorbing extremely nerdy contents of thesauri?

indicators.note: 'absorbing' means the jumbled letters take in the outer letters of nerdy
'possibly' hints that the letters could be arranged another way
'extremely' takes the extreme letters, first and last, of nerdy

explanation.surface: A parent musing that their bookish sons are soaking up the contents of word books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns MY SONS into SYNOMS, and NY goes inside: SYNO-NY-MS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus lists words of similar meaning, which is what this answer names.

clue.text: Broke wind by military bigwig

parts.note: the bora is a cold north-east wind of the Adriatic
CIC is commander-in-chief

explanation.surface: A senior officer passing wind and ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Boracic is British rhyming slang: boracic lint = skint, meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless, in British rhyming slang, so it means having no money at all.

clue.text: Heavyweight filling in expert without delay

indicators.note: the weight word fills the inside of the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavy boxer stepping in for a champion immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, straight away.

clue.text: Odious type interminably dominating servant without exception

indicators.note: in a down entry, dominating means sitting above, so the shortened word comes first
'interminably' means the word for the odious type loses its final letter

parts.note: a toad is a loathsome person
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A loathsome boss endlessly lording it over a servant, never letting up.
explanation.definitionFit: 'To a man' means every single one, with nobody left out.

clue.text: Old Nixon's a criminal — at least Blair and Clinton are these

definitions.text: at least Blair and Clinton are these

indicators.note: 'criminal' suggests something bent, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: Old Nixon was a crook, while at least two other leaders are something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair and Bill Clinton both studied at Oxford University (Clinton as a Rhodes Scholar).
explanation.definitionFit: Oxonians are people educated at Oxford, which includes both former leaders.

clue.text: Blunt heads of overseas bank taking on employment

indicators.note: 'heads of' takes the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: use means employment, as in 'put to use'

explanation.surface: Bluntly put, the chiefs of a foreign bank are hiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse can mean not sharp, rounded, as with a blunt edge or an angle over ninety degrees.

clue.text: Dismantles stars in play?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as three words, an actor accepts a role in a show

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as TAKES A PART to see the actor's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means breaking something into components, or literally accepting a role on stage.

clue.text: Weird mineral reduced in mass

indicators.note: 'reduced in' means the mineral loses the letter for mass

parts.note: emery is a hard rock used as an abrasive
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A strange rock that has lost weight.
explanation.walkthrough: EERY is a variant spelling of eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Eery, usually spelt eerie, means strange and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Gains by Labour picked up in ballot boxes

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: one earns by working, gaining through labour

explanation.surface: Electoral gains for the Labour Party found in the ballot boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the UK political party; here it means work. In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient voting, votes were cast into urns, so the word serves for ballot boxes.

clue.text: Damn bad weather heading for Iraq from a Gulf state

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of annoyance, like damn
rain is bad weather

indicators.note: 'heading for' takes the first letter of Iraq

explanation.surface: Cursing the foul weather on the way to Iraq from a neighbouring country.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahraini is the adjective for Bahrain, an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Sexy Posh perhaps wearing Sporty's or Scary's clothing

indicators.note: the outer letters are worn around the team, enclosing it

parts.note: the outside letters of either Sporty or Scary are S and Y
the Posh is the nickname of Peterborough United football team

explanation.surface: Posh Spice in Sporty or Scary Spice's outfit, from the Spice Girls.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls names mislead: the Posh is the nickname of Peterborough United, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy means erotic or passionate, describing something sexually charged.
